resources.name: Stock Research Agent
resources.description:
Ordered test flow. Run folders top to bottom: 00 -> 06.
Folders 00-03 need no OpenAI key (guardrails short-circuit, retrieval is embedding-only). Folder 04 makes real completion calls.

resources.name: 00 - Health and docs
resources.description: Confirm the app, database and migrations are live before anything else.

resources.name: 01 - Guardrails
resources.description: No OpenAI key needed: these short-circuit before the model call. Expect HTTP 200 with guardrailBlocked=true.

resources.name: 02 - Ingest filings
resources.description: Upload, dedup, and inventory. Needs an embedding model (OpenAI key or the embed-ollama profile).

resources.name: 03 - Retrieval only
resources.description: Raw vector search, no completion call. The cheapest way to see what the agent would retrieve.

resources.name: 04 - Ask the agent
resources.description: Real completion calls. Needs a working OPENAI_API_KEY.

resources.name: 05 - Cleanup
resources.description: Remove a filing and its chunks.

resources.name: 06 - Sandbox
resources.description: Local Ollama tool-calling playground. Not part of the agent.

resources.name: Health (all components)
resources.description:
Expect status UP with five components:
  db            -> the pgvector container on 5433
  filingCorpus  -> empty:true before you ingest anything
  marketData    -> a live AAPL price, proving the Yahoo feed works
  liveness/readinessState -> UP

If db is DOWN, the pgvector container is not running:
  docker start pgvector

resources.name: Liquibase changesets
resources.description:
Expect 8 changesets, all execType EXECUTED:
  001-extension-vector / -uuid
  002-filing-document / -indexes
  003-vectors-openai / -ollama
  004-metadata-indexes-openai / -ollama

resources.name: OpenAPI document
resources.description:
The spec behind Swagger UI at /swagger-ui.html.
Insomnia can import this directly (Import > URL) if you'd rather generate requests from it.

resources.name: BLOCKED - investment advice
resources.description:
Expect HTTP 200 (not 4xx) with:
  "guardrailBlocked": true
  "guardrailCategory": "INVESTMENT_ADVICE"
  "elapsedMillis": single digits  <- no model call was made

200-not-4xx is deliberate: a refusal is a valid conversational turn. Clients should branch on guardrailBlocked, not on the status code.

resources.name: BLOCKED - prompt injection
resources.description:
Expect guardrailCategory "PROMPT_INJECTION" and elapsedMillis near 0.

The reason it tripped is logged server-side but never returned - telling a prospective attacker which pattern matched makes the next attempt easier.

resources.name: BLOCKED - oversized input
resources.description: Expect HTTP 400 with problem type "validation-failed" (Bean Validation catches it at 4000 chars before the guardrail does).

resources.name: ALLOWED - control (false-positive check)
resources.description:
Contains the word 'buy' but is not soliciting a recommendation, so it must NOT be blocked.

Expect guardrailBlocked:false. Without a valid OPENAI_API_KEY this then returns 502 model-auth-failed - which still proves the guardrail let it through.

resources.name: Guardrail metric
resources.description:
Run this after the blocks above. Expect COUNT matching how many you triggered, tagged by category.

Empty response before the first block: Micrometer registers the counter on first increment.

resources.name: Inventory (before)
resources.description: Expect filingCount 0 on a fresh database.

resources.name: Upload Apple_10K-2025.pdf
resources.description:
Metadata is derived from the FILENAME - no other fields needed.
  Apple_10K-2025.pdf -> company Apple, form 10-K, FY2025
The ticker is resolved from 'Apple' via Yahoo symbol search.

Expect HTTP 201:
  "status": "INGESTED"
  "sectionsDetected": 14
  "chunksStored": ~91
  "latestVersion": true
  "sections": ["Cover and front matter", "Item 1. Business", "Item 1A. Risk Factors", ...]

Check that sections list. One 'Full document' entry means the PDF is image-only and Tika got nothing - Tika does not OCR.

Takes 10-60s: every chunk is embedded.

If the file path is wrong, re-pick it in the Body tab.

resources.name: Upload the SAME file again (dedup)
resources.description:
Expect HTTP 201 but:
  "status": "DUPLICATE_SKIPPED"
  "message": "Identical content was already ingested ... Pass force=true to replace it."

Returns instantly - nothing re-parsed, nothing re-embedded. The key is SHA-256 of the raw bytes, enforced by a UNIQUE constraint in filing_document.

Note this rejects duplicate CONTENT, not new VERSIONS: a FY2026 10-K would be accepted alongside this one.

resources.name: Inventory (after)
resources.description:
Expect filingCount 1, totalChunks ~91, and the filing marked currentVersion:true.

>>> COPY THE documentId INTO THE ENVIRONMENT (document_id) - folder 05 needs it.

resources.name: Which versions exist
resources.description:
Expect fiscalYears [2025] and current ['AAPL 10-K FY2025'].

Ingest a second year to see version resolution pick the newer one automatically.

resources.name: Health (corpus now populated)
resources.description: filingCorpus should now show empty:false, documentsIndexed:1, and currentFilings ['AAPL 10-K FY2025'].

resources.name: Search - risk factors
resources.url: {{ _.base_url }}/api/filings/search?query=supply chain concentration and single source suppliers&ticker={{ _.ticker }}&topK=5
resources.description:
Raw vector search. One embedding call, NO completion - so this works even without a chat model, and it is the cheapest way to tune retrieval.

Expect hits from 'Item 1A. Risk Factors' with scores ~0.6-0.8, and documentsSearched showing which filing was in scope.

Each hit carries the metadata the agent cites from: ticker, form_type, fiscal_year, section.

resources.name: Search - MD&A
resources.url: {{ _.base_url }}/api/filings/search?query=revenue by segment and gross margin drivers&ticker={{ _.ticker }}&topK=5
resources.description:
Should hit 'Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis'.

Different section from the previous query - this is what section-aware chunking buys: chunks never straddle an Item boundary, so retrieval lands in the right part of the filing.

resources.name: Search - versionScope=ALL
resources.description:
With one filing ingested the result is identical to LATEST.

The difference appears once you ingest a second year: LATEST searches only the newest edition, ALL searches every version. Compare documentsSearched between this and the first request.

resources.name: Search - off-topic (threshold check)
resources.description:
Expect hitCount 0.

This is the similarity threshold (0.55) doing its job. Without it you would get the least-bad chunk in the corpus and the agent would answer confidently from irrelevant text. Nothing back is the correct answer here.

resources.name: Market data only
resources.description:
The agent calls searchStockSymbol then getStockQuote.

Expect a price with an as-of timestamp, and a 'not investment advice' disclaimer appended by the output guardrail.

502 model-auth-failed here means OPENAI_API_KEY is not valid.

resources.name: Filing only
resources.description:
The agent calls searchFilings (scoped to the latest 10-K) and answers with a citation like '(AAPL 10-K FY2025, Item 1A. Risk Factors)'.

It should NOT answer from general knowledge - the system prompt forbids it.

resources.name: Both sources in one turn
resources.description:
The interesting one: market data AND filings in a single answer, with the live price attributed to the tool timestamp and the filing claims cited to the document.

Watch the app log to see the tool-calling sequence.

resources.name: Honest 'I don't have that'
resources.description:
No Tesla filing has been ingested, so the agent must say the filing is not available rather than answering from memory.

This is the single most important behaviour to verify - it is what separates a grounded agent from one that sounds grounded.

resources.name: Document-only endpoint
resources.description:
No market tools on this path - the answer can only come from retrieved document text.

Note this searches ALL versions: the retrieval advisor has no parameters through which to express a version scope. Use /api/agent/ask when latest-only matters.

resources.name: Streaming
resources.description:
Server-sent events, one element per token fragment.

Note: the output disclaimer is NOT appended on this path - each element carries a fragment, so there is no complete answer to inspect before it is sent. Input guardrails still apply.

resources.name: Delete a filing
resources.description:
Set document_id in the environment first (from the inventory response).

Expect HTTP 204. Removes the registry row AND every chunk referencing it.

If this was the current edition, the next-newest becomes current automatically - nothing to update by hand, because 'latest' is resolved at query time.

resources.name: Ollama tool-calling sandbox
resources.url: {{ _.base_url }}/ai/ollama/chat?message=What is the current price of bitcoin?
resources.description:
Local model with a crypto price tool attached. Requires a running Ollama daemon.

Useful for checking that a tool's description and schema are clear enough to be called correctly, without paying for hosted inference on every iteration. Not part of the stock agent.

resources.name: 04b - Conversation memory
resources.description: Multi-turn follow-ups. Needs a working OPENAI_API_KEY. Run the three 'turn' requests IN ORDER, pasting conversationId into the environment after turn 1.

resources.name: Turn 1 - start a conversation
resources.description:
No conversationId in the body, so the server mints one.

>>> COPY conversationId FROM THE RESPONSE into the environment variable conversation_id. Turns 2 and 3 depend on it.

resources.name: Turn 2 - pronoun follow-up
resources.description:
The question says 'their' and never names Apple. It is only answerable because turn 1 is replayed into the prompt.

If the agent asks 'which company?', memory is not working - check that conversation_id is set and that jspringverse.memory.enabled=true.

resources.name: Turn 3 - reference an earlier number
resources.description: Refers back to the price from turn 1 without restating it. Tests that the assistant's own earlier answers are retained, not just the user's questions.

resources.name: Read the transcript
resources.description:
Exactly what would be replayed on the next turn, oldest first.

Expect alternating user/assistant entries. Only the last 40 messages are retained (jspringverse.memory.max-messages) - this is a window, not an audit log.

resources.name: List conversations
resources.description:
Every conversation id on the instance.

NOTE: no authorisation. Conversation ids are the only thing separating one caller's history from another's, so this endpoint hands out all of them. Remove it or put it behind authentication before more than one user can reach the app.

resources.name: Different conversation = clean slate
resources.description:
Same pronoun question, but on a DIFFERENT conversation id.

Expect the agent to have no idea who 'their' refers to - proving conversations are isolated and memory is not leaking across threads.

resources.name: Blocked questions stay out of history
resources.description:
Send this, then re-read the transcript above.

The refusal must NOT appear in the transcript. The guardrail advisor runs ahead of the memory advisor precisely so a blocked question is never persisted - otherwise the offending text would be replayed into the prompt on every later turn of this conversation.

resources.name: Forget the conversation
resources.description:
Expect HTTP 204. Irreversible.

Re-run 'Read the transcript' afterwards: messageCount should be 0, and a follow-up on the same id starts fresh.
